questions.explanation: With uniform hashing, the expected chain length equals the load factor α = n/m, so lookups take O(1 + α) on average. The worst case is O(n) when many keys collide, so claiming O(1) worst case is a common mistake.
options: O(1) in the worst case, because every key hashes to its own bucket
O(n) in every case, because the chains must be scanned from the head
O(1) on average, since the expected chain length is the load factor n/8, which stays constant when n is fixed relative to the table size
O(log n), because the chains are kept sorted like a balanced tree
questions.question: A hash table uses separate chaining with a fixed array of 8 buckets. Which statement best describes the expected cost of a successful lookup when the table holds n keys and the hash function spreads them uniformly?

questions.explanation: An in-order traversal of a binary search tree visits the left subtree, the node, then the right subtree, which yields the keys in sorted ascending order. The other options reflect pre-order, post-order, or reversed traversals.
questions.question: Consider a binary search tree built by inserting the keys 50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80 in that order. What is the in-order traversal of this tree?

questions.explanation: Big-O keeps only the dominant term and drops constant coefficients, so 3n^2 + 10n + 500 is O(n^2). Writing O(3n^2) or O(n^2 + n) keeps constants or lower-order terms that Big-O is designed to ignore.
questions.question: An algorithm performs about 3n^2 + 10n + 500 basic operations on an input of size n. Which expression is its asymptotic bound in Big-O notation?
